UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile within the application, storing supplementary information beyond basic authentication. Authentication details are managed externally by Firebase Authentication.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. (Primary Key)

displayName.description: The user's display name or full name.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Transcript.title: Transcript
Transcript.description: Stores the content of a meeting transcript submitted by a user for action item extraction.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transcript entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who submitted this transcript. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Transcript)

title.description: An optional title or brief description for the meeting transcript.

content.description: The full text content of the meeting transcript.

submittedAt.description: Timestamp when the transcript was submitted.

Task.title: Task
Task.description: Represents an action item extracted from a meeting transcript by the AI processing pipeline.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Task entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns this task. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Task)

transcriptId.description: Reference to the Transcript from which this task was extracted. (Relationship: Transcript 1:N Task)

description.description: A clear description of the action item or task.

owner.description: The person or entity assigned to complete the task.

deadline.description: The specified deadline for the task, could be a date or a relative time (e.g., 'by Monday', 'this week').

priority.description: Categorical priority level of the task (e.g., 'HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW').

priorityScore.description: Numerical priority score for the task, ranging from 0 to 100.

confidenceScore.description: The AI model's confidence in the extraction of this task, ranging from 0 to 100.

sourceSentence.description: The original sentence from the transcript from which the task was extracted.

status.description: The current status of the task (e.g., 'pending', 'completed').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the task was extracted and created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the task was last updated (e.g., status change, edit).

Run.title: Run
Run.description: Records the metadata and high-level results of a single AI processing run for a meeting transcript.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Run entity, also referred to as Run ID. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who initiated this processing run. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Run)

transcriptId.description: Reference to the Transcript that was processed during this run. (Relationship: Transcript 1:N Run)

startedAt.description: Timestamp when the AI processing run started.

completedAt.description: Timestamp when the AI processing run was completed, regardless of success or failure.

status.description: The overall status of the processing run (e.g., 'PENDING', 'COMPLETED', 'FAILED').

totalTasksExtracted.description: The total number of action items extracted during this run.

averageConfidenceScore.description: The average confidence score of all tasks extracted in this run.

processingTimeMs.description: The total processing time for this run in milliseconds.

errorDetails.description: Details of any error that occurred during the run, if applicable.

finalResultsSummary.description: A summary of the final results produced by the AI workflow.

LogEvent.title: LogEvent
LogEvent.description: Captures a single timestamped event or state transition within an AI processing workflow run.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LogEvent entity. (Primary Key)

runId.description: Reference to the Run entity this log event belongs to. (Relationship: Run 1:N LogEvent)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile associated with the run that generated this log event. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N LogEvent)

timestamp.description: Timestamp when this log event occurred.

eventType.description: The type of event being logged (e.g., 'STATE_TRANSITION', 'TOOL_CALL', 'INFO', 'WARNING', 'ERROR').

message.description: A human-readable message describing the log event.

fromState.description: The state from which the workflow transitioned, if eventType is 'STATE_TRANSITION'.

toState.description: The state to which the workflow transitioned, if eventType is 'STATE_TRANSITION'.

toolName.description: The name of the tool or service that was called, if eventType is 'TOOL_CALL'.

details.description: Additional JSON-stringified details or context relevant to this specific log event.

errorDetails.description: Specific error information if the eventType is 'ERROR'.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes strict user-based ownership and authorization independence, adhering to the core design principles. All user-specific data is nested under a top-level `/users/{userId}` collection. This strategy creates an explicit, intuitive hierarchy that mirrors the application's single-user data ownership model.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** Each document (`UserProfile`, `Transcript`, `Task`, `Run`, `LogEvent`) is designed to contain its `userId` (and `runId` for `LogEvent`) directly within the document data itself, in addition to being part of its path. For example, a `Task` document located at `/users/{userId}/tasks/{taskId}` will also have a `userId` field within its data. This denormalization is crucial: Firebase Security Rules can check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` without needing a `get()` operation to a parent document or a separate user profile, thus enabling atomic operations and simplifying rule logic. This completely eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies, making rules robust and easily debuggable.

**Clarity of Intent (Debuggability):** The path structure `users/{userId}/...` explicitly states that all data within this segment belongs to the specified user. This makes authorization rules incredibly clear (e.g., `allow read, write: request.auth.uid == userId;`).

**DBAC (No Custom Claims):** User roles (if any were present) would be stored as fields within the `UserProfile` document, but in this application, all data is private to the user, so no roles beyond owner are required.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** By segregating all user data under `/users/{userId}/...`, list operations inherently retrieve only the authenticated user's data. For instance, a query on `/users/{request.auth.uid}/tasks` will only return tasks owned by the current user. The security rules will enforce that `request.auth.uid` matches the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, ensuring that `list` operations are implicitly filtered by the security context, satisfying the QAP principle without requiring complex `where` clauses in rules.

**Structural Segregation:** Each collection (`/users`, `/users/{userId}/transcripts`, `/users/{userId}/tasks`, `/users/{userId}/runs`, `/users/{userId}/runs/{runId}/logEvents`) holds documents with a homogeneous security posture – they are all privately owned by the associated user. This prevents mixing data with different access requirements, further simplifying security rules.

**Access Modeling:** The design exclusively uses Path-Based ownership (`/users/{userId}/data`) and continues this hierarchy for nested data (`/users/{userId}/runs/{runId}/logEvents`). This is the most secure and straightforward model for private user data.
